transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alicia Varga (SynerTech Head of ML), Marcus Lee (SynerTech Platform Eng), Diane Wu (SynerTech CTO)

Summary: quick parity walkthrough mapping their OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to Redwood API, cover console routing, and Optimize recommendations for cost and latency. Some noisy transcription; filler words and interruptions present.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, good afternoon, thanks for joining. this is jordan from Redwood. we have priya on the call as well, our solutions engineer. quick confirm—can you hear me okay?
[00:07] Alicia: yep, I can hear you. thanks. sorry about the time zones, a bit of back and forth today.
[00:12] Marcus: all good, i've got diane on my side too. we'll try to stay high level then drill where needed.
[00:20] Jordan: perfect. objective today: map parity for your three main endpoints (chat->openai gpt, completion-ish anthroic and a together.ll model), show the console, and go over Optimize recommendations for cost and latency. also figure next steps for a bench test. sound right?
[00:36] Alicia: sounds good. we're most concerned about latency for our live chat product and cost for nightly batch summarization jobs.
[00:44] Priya: cool. before we map, can you share a quick overview of your current stack? Marcus?
[00:50] Marcus: sure. current prod uses OpenAI for chat, Anthropic for safety sensitive flows, and Together for some on-prem-ish models. we proxy everything through our api gateway, run k8s in us-west-2, and keep KV cache in redis. we also have a tiny edge cache for prefixes. retention rules: logs kept 90 days, PII stripped.
[01:12] Diane: also our SLOs: p95 < 160ms for chat inference (token-limited), nightly batch can be 3–4 hours, cost target is reducing token spend by at least 30% vs current spend.
[01:26] Jordan: ok that's helpful. quick note: when we say p95 we mean the server-side inference only—we'll map network overhead separately. Redwood's routing can pin to region and model variants, and we have dedicated pools if you need guaranteed latency.
[01:45] Priya: i'll jump into parity mapping. i've got your sample payloads from the spreadsheet you attached—great—i'll walk through a direct mapping: OpenAI "chat.completions" -> Redwood /v1/chat.generate, Anthropic style -> Redwood conversational endpoint with safety hooks, Together -> Redwood model variant with lower precision quant profile. a couple of caveats: Together's RT optimizations for large context windows sometimes rely on custom kernels that we emulate with quantized kernels; that can change per-token lat slightly.
[02:20] Alicia: wait, does that mean latency could go up after quantization? i thought quant reduces cost and usually helps latency.
[02:26] Priya: good question. in many cases quant reduces GPU memory and can improve throughput; but for single-request low-latency p95 you can see different behavior depending on batching. with continuous batching and our prefix/K-V caching, we've seen p95 be stable or improved. but there are rare cases where kernel selection leads to small bump—usually 10–20ms.
[02:50] Marcus: that's acceptable if overall cost drops. can you show me where in the console we tune batching and cache?
[02:56] Jordan: sure — i'll share my screen. (link to console) -- NOTE: shared artifacts: https://redwood.app/parity/synertech-parity-2026.csv and the cost model: https://redwood.app/costs/synertech-first-pass.xlsx

[03:20] Priya: on screen now — console route config, you can set per-route model selection, fallback tiers (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and token-level cost caps. here's where Optimize suggestions surface: batch window, target batch size, and quantization profile recommendations for each endpoint.
[03:40] Alicia: can you run through an example mapping for our chat endpoint? like exact config?
[03:45] Priya: yes. route: /chat/live maps to model: rwd-gpt-7b-chat (we'd pick based on your quality evals), with session affinity TTL 60s, kv_cache enabled for prefix reuse, batching window 15ms for p95 target, and auto-fallback to rwd-gpt-7b_chat_q4 for cost-burst scenarios. in the spreadsheet we lined up response shapes to match your current OpenAI schema—there's a token_delta field we add for billing parity.
[04:26] Speaker 1: um, there's some background noise — sorry if the transcription gets messy here.
[04:31] Jordan: no worries. another thing is routing policy — you can route by customer tier (prod vs dev) or by latency requirement. so prod chat hits dedicated pool with reserved GPUs and strict SLOs, dev hits hosted.
[04:50] Marcus: if we go dedicated for chat, what's minimum commitment?
[04:54] Jordan: typical reserved capacity starts at one GPU pod equivalent for 3 months minimum; pricing details in the sheet but we usually model a break-even within 8–12 weeks for chat-heavy workloads.
[05:10] Diane: and for compliance — SOC2 / SSO stuff — we need audit logs and HSM integration.
[05:16] Jordan: yes, private deployment supports KMS/HSM and audit logs. our enterprise package includes longer retention and SSO via SAML/Okta. we'll send detailed security slide deck after.
[05:28] Alicia: great. what's the plan for running the bench tests — can we do a side-by-side token-level comparison?
[05:35] Priya: absolutely. typical bench: 2-hour scheduled run in your region using a replay of 24 hours worth of traffic (sampled): chat workload at 100 rps spikes, batch jobs during off hours. we run parallel runs: your OpenAI/Anthropic/Together baseline and Redwood endpoints, measure p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and failure modes. results go into the cost model sheet.
[06:05] Marcus: what about model equivalence? our safety hooks rely on Anthropic tooling.
[06:10] Priya: we can wire similar safety checks at the route level — prefilters, wrapper policies, and token-level reranking. Redwood also supports function/tool calling so you can normalise safety outputs. note transcription sometimes wrote "Anthropic" as "Anthrotpic" on the notes — ignore that.
[06:30] Alicia: ha, ok. can you talk about KV cache invalidation? we have a lot of short-lived sessions.
[06:36] Priya: yes — you can set kv cache TTL per route. for short sessions we recommend short TTLs (30–60s) and prefix caching to keep latency down. also our continuous batching respects session affinity to avoid cross-talk.
[06:52] Jordan: quick interjection — cost sanity checks. in the first-pass spreadsheet we model two scenarios: aggressive quant (q4) and conservative (q8) and show cost delta. aggressive quant can cut inference cost by ~40% but might change token-level logprobs—so you need evals.
[07:14] Alicia: i want to avoid regressions in NLU accuracy. do you support A/B rollouts for model variants?
[07:19] Priya: yes, rollout features in the console: canary % routing, A/B by user cohort, and auto-fallback rules if quality metrics drop beyond a threshold. we tie to evals to detect regressions.
[07:35] Marcus: any gotchas with Together integrations? we do some local caching & kernel tweaks today.
[07:40] Priya: Together tends to use custom CUDA kernels for long-context. our runtime uses kernel selection logic; for dev we map to compatible kernels and enable a quant profile. we'll flag any mismatches in the parity sheet and propose micro-benchmarks.
[08:02] Speaker 2: small delay on my side — lagging by a sec.
[08:05] Jordan: okay let's pivot to the Optimize suggestions — two quick wins we highlighted: intelligent batching for peak hours and prefix caching for chat threads. those typically provide the largest cost-per-token reduction without quality loss.
[08:22] Priya: on the screen — Optimize dashboard. it lists candidate routes with potential savings, suggested batch window, and expected latency impact. you can apply recommendations per-route or at account level.
[08:36] Alicia: can we auto-apply in a staging environment first?
[08:39] Priya: yes, there's a staging toggle. we can run recommended settings in stage for X hours and collect metrics before promotion.
[08:46] Marcus: curious about token accounting — if we cache prefixes, do we still bill for cached tokens?
[08:52] Jordan: we bill for tokens emitted; cache saves compute but cached tokens are not recomputed so they reduce billed compute. there are nuances—client-side logging might show token counts differently; we'll reconcile in the bench results.
[09:08] Diane: what's your observability story? we need traceability for token-level cost, prompt outputs, and user-level SLOs.
[09:15] Priya: console provides per-route token breakdown, trace IDs linkable to logs, and we can stream traces to your ingestion (Datadog/Splunk). plus tracing hooks for eval diffs.
[09:30] Jordan: quick Q — any constraints on bringing data into your VPC? you said you have some on-prem Together flow.
[09:38] Marcus: our on-prem models cannot leave the VPC; we'd need a private Redwood deployment or an air-gapped option for that subset.
[09:46] Priya: that's supported — private deployment package works with on-prem inference, and the control plane can be customer-managed. there are a few setup steps: network peering, cert rotations, and KMS hookups.
[10:02] Alicia: ok. this is great. let's talk timeline. ideally we'd run a bench in 2 weeks and get initial results in 3.
[10:10] Jordan: sounds reasonable. i'll put the tentative dates in next steps.

--- mid-call technical deep dive (notes clipped / transcription noisy) ---
[10:20] Priya: diving into bench harness — we recommend using our bench runner; it's a container you run in your cluster which replays payloads and collects metrics. you'll need to attach a service account and set the target routes.
[10:36] Marcus: for the bench runner do you need us to push sample logs? we can export 24h of traffic to S3.
[10:42] Priya: yes S3 export works. we also accept direct streaming to the harness if you prefer. format: newline-delimited JSON with timestamp, request_id, user_id, payload.
[10:56] Alicia: small note — some of our requests include attachments; do you support multimodal?
[11:02] Priya: we do for supported models; for benching we usually strip attachments and focus on text path first. we can add a small attachment subset later.
[11:12] Jordan: ok rounding into recap soon — but any last must-have constraints?
[11:18] Diane: encryption keys—if we do private, we need HSM-backed keys and dedicated audit delivery.
[11:24] Jordan: noted. i'll add that to the security pack we'll send.

[11:30] Priya: quick live demo of the parity sheet — mapping table shows: source endpoint, request shape differences, recommended Redwood endpoint, quant suggestion, expected cost delta, and risk level. e.g., OpenAI chat -> rwd-gpt-7b-chat (q8), expected -28% cost; Anthropic safety flow -> rwd-safety-tier (q4) expected -33% cost with safety hooks; Together long-context -> rwd-ctx-variant (q4o) expected -20% but flagged for kernel mismatch.
[12:05] Marcus: can we get the sheet as a CSV? easier to import.
[12:08] Jordan: yes, we'll post CSV. link again: https://redwood.app/parity/synertech-parity-2026.csv

[12:20] Alicia: let's confirm next steps and owners.
[12:24] Jordan: next steps: 1) Jordan share parity CSV + cost scenarios by 2026-10-01. 2) Priya schedule 2-hour bench in us-west-2, share runner instructions by 2026-10-03. 3) SynerTech to grant sample endpoints + S3 bucket with logs by 2026-10-06. 4) Redwood to send security/enterprise deck (SOC2, SAML, HSM) by 2026-10-02.
[12:55] Diane: ok agreed. any blockers on our side? we need internal signoff for network peering.
[13:01] Marcus: i'll start the ticket, should be fine.

[13:10] Jordan: perfect. i'll follow up with calendar invites and the documents. thanks everyone.
[13:16] Alicia: thanks you all.
[13:18] Diane: thanks.

Transcript end. Notes: minor transcription glitches (speaker swaps, mis-spelled vendors: "Anthrotpic", "togethr"), removed long code snippets. Shared artifacts referenced but not included.
